exposure: maternal age (adolescent vs. adult, and younger vs. older teenage deliveries)
cohort: This study included 3,614,274 livebirths from a linked maternal-infant database in Florida, comparing adolescent pregnancies (10-19 years old) to adult deliveries (ages 25-29 as reference) from 2000 to 2019.
finding: Adolescent mothers, especially the youngest teens, are at increased risk for adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes including fetal growth restriction, low birth weight, preterm birth, respiratory distress syndrome, neonatal/infant death, maternal sepsis, and hypertensive disorders.
mod_finding: Teenage deliveries were less likely to result in a cesarean birth.
followup_time: Up to 1 year after birth (indicated by 'neonatal/infant death')
birth_weight: low birth weight, fetal growth restriction (no specific weight ranges mentioned)
gest_age: preterm birth (no specific gestational age ranges mentioned)
